header.title: Ad equum errehet (Paris, Bibl. Nationale, Ms. nouv. acq. lat. 229): AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Anonymous
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:rem:anonymous:m001:norm, from the Referenzkorpus Mittelhochdeutsch, ReM 2.1 (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.

notes.2: 'erræhet' is foundered (laminitis). *êrngrehte* (2.4) is obscure: perhaps a retinue, or harvest gear. 'bî viere' (2.9) is unclear: 'by fours', 'four times', or 'by the fire' (viure). The word 'rosse' (horse) stands at the start of 2.15; it is moved up into 2.14 for English order. Colours: 'rôt' red or bay, 'vale' dun or fallow, 'vêch' dappled or pied.

nodes.text: A man went along the road,
then it will be cured of the founder.'
The Our Father. And wipe its legs and feet, saying: As quickly may
this horse, whatever its colour, red, black, white, dun, grey, dappled,
be cured of the founder as the one that God cured there.
